solution:
Factorise the numerator: \((\sqrt{x} + \sqrt{1+x})\,\sqrt{1+x} = \sqrt{x}\,\sqrt{1+x} + (1+x) = 1 + x + \sqrt{x + x^2}\), which is exactly the numerator.

So the integrand reduces to \(\dfrac{(\sqrt{x} + \sqrt{1+x})\,\sqrt{x+1}}{\sqrt{x} + \sqrt{1+x}} = \sqrt{x+1}\).

Hence \(\displaystyle\int \sqrt{x+1}\,dx = \dfrac{2}{3}(x+1)^{3/2} + c\).

Check: \(\dfrac{d}{dx}\left[\dfrac{2}{3}(x+1)^{3/2}\right] = \sqrt{x+1}\), the integrand.

Hence (B).

Add the two integrals: \(\int\frac{1}{x+x^5}dx+\int\frac{x^4}{x+x^5}dx=\int\frac{1+x^4}{x(1+x^4)}dx=\int\frac{1}{x}dx=\log x\). Since the first integral is \(f(x)\), the required integral \(=\log x-f(x)+c\). Answer A.

Write \(\log(3x)=\log x+\log 3\) and \(\log(9x)=\log x+\log 9=\log x+2\log 3\). Put \(t=\log(9x)\), \(dt=\frac{1}{x}dx\); then \(\log(3x)=t-\log 3\), so the integral is \(\int\frac{t-\log 3}{t}dt=t-(\log 3)\log t=\log(9x)-(\log 3)\log(\log 9x)\). Since \(\log(9x)\) differs from \(\log x\) by the constant \(\log 9\), this equals \(\log x-(\log 3)\cdot\log(\log 9x)+c\). Differentiating option B reproduces the integrand exactly. Answer B.

\(\frac{\sin^m x}{\cos^{m+2}x}=\frac{\sin^m x}{\cos^m x}\cdot\frac{1}{\cos^2 x}=\tan^m x\,\sec^2 x\). With \(t=\tan x\), \(dt=\sec^2 x\,dx\), integral \(=\int t^m dt=\frac{\tan^{m+1}x}{m+1}+c\). Verified for \(m=3\): \(\frac{d}{dx}\frac{\tan^{m+1}x}{m+1}=\tan^m x\sec^2 x\). Answer A.

\(\tan(\sin^{-1}x)=\frac{\sin(\sin^{-1}x)}{\cos(\sin^{-1}x)}=\frac{x}{\sqrt{1-x^2}}\). Put \(u=1-x^2\), \(du=-2x\,dx\); \(\int\frac{x}{\sqrt{1-x^2}}dx=-\sqrt{1-x^2}+c\). Differentiating option D gives \(\frac{x}{\sqrt{1-x^2}}\), matching. Answer D.

Using \(1-\cos x=2\sin^2(x/2)\) and \(\sin x=2\sin(x/2)\cos(x/2)\): \(\frac{x-\sin x}{1-\cos x}=\frac{x}{2}\csc^2\frac{x}{2}-\cot\frac{x}{2}\). Integrate \(\frac{x}{2}\csc^2\frac{x}{2}\) by parts (\(u=x\), \(dv=\frac12\csc^2\frac{x}{2}dx\Rightarrow v=-\cot\frac{x}{2}\)): \(=-x\cot\frac{x}{2}+\int\cot\frac{x}{2}dx\). The \(\int\cot\frac{x}{2}dx\) cancels the \(-\int\cot\frac{x}{2}dx\) remaining term, leaving \(-x\cot\frac{x}{2}+c\). Differentiation of option B confirms it. Answer B.

With \(t=\sin^{-1}x\), \(f(x)g(x)dx=t\,e^{t}\,dt\). Integration by parts: \(\int t\,e^t dt=e^t(t-1)=e^{\sin^{-1}x}(\sin^{-1}x-1)+c\). Differentiating this returns the integrand. DEFECTIVE MCQ: options A and D are printed identically (\(e^{\sin^{-1}x}(\sin^{-1}x-1)+c\)) and both are correct; the intended correct choice is the first one, A.

\(\int\tan^3 x\sec^3 x\,dx=\int\tan^2 x\sec^2 x(\sec x\tan x)dx=\int(\sec^2 x-1)\sec^2 x\,d(\sec x)\) with \(u=\sec x\): \(\int(u^4-u^2)du=\frac{u^5}{5}-\frac{u^3}{3}=\frac{1}{5}\sec^5 x-\frac{1}{3}\sec^3 x+c\). Comparing with \(\frac{1}{m}\sec^m x-\frac{1}{n}\sec^n x\) gives \((m,n)=(5,3)\). Answer A.

\(\frac{1}{\cos x-\cos^2 x}=\frac{1}{\cos x(1-\cos x)}=\frac{1}{\cos x}+\frac{1}{1-\cos x}\) (partial fractions in \(\cos x\)). Then \(\int\sec x\,dx=\log(\sec x+\tan x)\) and \(\int\frac{dx}{1-\cos x}=\int\frac12\csc^2\frac{x}{2}dx=-\cot\frac{x}{2}\). Sum \(=\log(\sec x+\tan x)-\cot\frac{x}{2}+c\). Differentiation of option C reproduces the integrand exactly. Answer C.

\(\frac{\sqrt{\cot x}}{\sin x\cos x}=\sqrt{\cot x}\cdot\frac{\sec^2 x}{\tan x}=\frac{\sec^2 x}{(\cot x)^{1/2}\tan x}\). Put \(t=\cot x\), \(dt=-\csc^2 x\,dx\); the integrand becomes \(-t^{-1/2}dt\), giving \(-2\sqrt{t}=-2\sqrt{\cot x}+c\). Differentiating option B returns the integrand. Answer B.

\(\frac{e^x(x-1)}{x^2}=e^x\left(\frac{1}{x}-\frac{1}{x^2}\right)=e^x\left(\frac1x+\frac{d}{dx}\frac1x\right)\). By the \(\int e^x(f+f')=e^x f\) rule with \(f=\frac1x\), integral \(=\frac{e^x}{x}+c\). Differentiating option A gives \(\frac{e^x(x-1)}{x^2}\). Answer A.
\(\int\sin(\log x)dx\): put \(x=e^t\), \(dx=e^t dt\), \(=\int e^t\sin t\,dt=\frac{e^t}{2}(\sin t-\cos t)=\frac{x}{2}[\sin(\log x)-\cos(\log x)]+c\). Differentiation of option A confirms it. Answer A.
Since \(\frac{d}{dx}x^x=x^x(1+\log x)\), the integrand is exactly \(\frac{d}{dx}x^x\), so \(\int x^x(1+\log x)dx=x^x+c\). Answer D.

\(\cos^{-3/7}x\,\sin^{-11/7}x=\frac{\sec^2 x}{\tan^{11/7}x}\) (since \(\cos^{-3/7}\sin^{-11/7}=\cos^{-2}\cdot(\tan)^{-11/7}\)). Put \(t=\tan x\): \(\int t^{-11/7}dt=\frac{t^{-4/7}}{-4/7}=-\frac{7}{4}\tan^{-4/7}x+c\). Differentiating option C returns the integrand (verified numerically to machine precision). Answer C.
Denominator \(\cos^2 x+\sin^2 x=1\) and numerator \(\cos^2 x-\sin^2 x=\cos 2x\), so \(2\int\cos 2x\,dx=2\cdot\frac{\sin 2x}{2}=\sin 2x+c\). Answer A.

Divide numerator and denominator inside by \(\cos^2 x\): \(\frac{1}{\cos x\sqrt{\sin^2 x-\cos^2 x}}=\frac{\sec^2 x}{\sqrt{\tan^2 x-1}}\). Put \(t=\tan x\), \(dt=\sec^2 x\,dx\): \(\int\frac{dt}{\sqrt{t^2-1}}=\log\!\left(t+\sqrt{t^2-1}\right)=\log\!\left(\tan x+\sqrt{\tan^2 x-1}\right)+c\). Differentiating option D reproduces the integrand (verified numerically on the valid domain \(x\in(\pi/4,\pi/2)\)). Answer D.

\(\log(ex)=1+\log x\), so integrand \(=\frac{\log x}{(1+\log x)^2}=\frac{(1+\log x)-1}{(1+\log x)^2}=\frac{1}{1+\log x}-\frac{1}{(1+\log x)^2}\). This is \(e^t\)-type form under \(x=e^t\): \(\int e^t\left(\frac{1}{1+t}-\frac{1}{(1+t)^2}\right)dt=\frac{e^t}{1+t}=\frac{x}{1+\log x}+c\). Differentiating option A returns the integrand. Answer A.
\(\frac{d}{dx}\big(x\sin(\log x)\big)=\sin(\log x)+x\cos(\log x)\cdot\frac1x=\sin(\log x)+\cos(\log x)\), exactly the integrand. Hence \(\int[\sin(\log x)+\cos(\log x)]dx=x\sin(\log x)+c\). Answer D.
\(\cos 2x-1=-2\sin^2 x\), \(\cos 2x+1=2\cos^2 x\), so integrand \(=-\tan^2 x=-(\sec^2 x-1)=1-\sec^2 x\). Integrating: \(x-\tan x+c\). Answer C.
\(\frac{e^{2x}+e^{-2x}}{e^x}=e^{x}+e^{-3x}\). Integrate: \(e^x+\frac{e^{-3x}}{-3}=e^x-\frac{1}{3e^{3x}}+c\). Differentiating option A returns the integrand. Answer A.
